clearedSpotChecks.check: EIP-7702 on Avalanche C-Chain: a call into an account whose code is a delegation designator. Avalanche fails the call and reports EXTCODESIZE 23, where the other 20 networks follow the delegation.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Rerun by the verifier with eth_call and state overrides at latest: caller 0xc0 CALLs 0xa0 whose code is 0xef0100 followed by 0xb0, and 0xb0 returns the word 42. Avalanche (api.avax.network) gives status 0, return data size 0, EXTCODESIZE 23. Ethereum (ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com) and Monad (rpc.monad.xyz) give status 1, return data 42 of 32 bytes, EXTCODESIZE 23. The PoolManager reaches outside code only through hook calls (src/libraries/Hooks.sol) and currency transfers (src/types/Currency.sol); a designator account on Avalanche would make such a call fail and revert the caller's own transaction, which hurts no other user. EIP-3541 stops ordinary deployment of code that starts with 0xef, so no account an attacker can make on Avalanche carries a designator.

clearedSpotChecks.check: The rest of pyevm.py, opcode by opcode against the Cancun specification for gas-independent results (SDIV, SMOD, SLT, SGT, SAR, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, SHL, SHR, MULMOD, ADDMOD and EXP at their edges, MCOPY overlap in both directions and more): pyevm.py gives the chain's answer on every case on all 21 networks apart from the listed faults.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Independent battery by the verifier, written from the Yellow Paper definitions in Python and not from pyevm.py: 42 edge vectors (SDIV of -2^255 by -1 and by 0, SMOD with negative operands, ADDMOD and MULMOD with full-width operands and moduli 2^256-2 and 2^160+7, EXP with exponent 2^256-1 and 2^256 overflow, SIGNEXTEND with byte index 30, 31 and 2^255, SAR by 255, 256 and 2^256-1 of negative values, SHL and SHR by 255 and 256, BYTE at 31, 32 and 2^256-1, SLT and SGT at the sign boundary, DIV and MOD by 0) plus MCOPY overlap forward by 3 bytes and backward by 10 bytes, run by eth_call at latest on chains 1, 42220, 196, 56, 43114, 143, 4326, 4217, 5042 and 999. Every network returned the expected value for all 42 vectors and the expected memory for both copies. These are the operations FullMath.mulDiv, UnsafeMath, BitMath, TickMath and SqrtPriceMath rely on, so no difference reaches src/libraries through them on those ten networks.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Reference interpreter fault 1, stack limit: tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:102-110 handles PUSH1 to PUSH32, DUP1 to DUP16 and PUSH0 with continue, which skips the only overflow check at pyevm.py:218. No PoolManager comparison can rest on the fault.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read tools/opdiff/pyevm.py: the PUSH (0x60-0x7f), DUP (0x80-0x8f) and PUSH0 (0x5f) branches append and continue before the check `if len(st) > 1024: raise Halt('stack overflow')` at the end of the loop body, so those pushes are never checked. The same file also confirms fault 3 (address 1 returns empty for input under 128 bytes, pyevm.py:72-73) and fault 4 (snapshot at pyevm.py:57-58 holds storage, transient storage and balances but not self.logs). The argument that the fault can only turn a chain halt into a reference success, which shows as a mismatch and never hides one, holds: an extra success adds state or return data that the chain lacks. The 49 item maximum was not remeasured by the verifier.
